course_description: This course provides a practical introduction to emerging music technologies and their use by musicians and music educators across a range of contexts, including the classroom and studio. The focus of this course is the examination of emerging approaches to the use of music technology and the completion of creative music technology projects related to audio production, sound creation and performance. Students will develop skills for negotiating new apps and technologies. Students will also learn how to record, mix, and produce audio and MIDI through a series of practical and creative production tasks. By the end of the course, students will have developed a range of creative and technical skills for creating and performing music, which are applicable across professional and classroom contexts. Please note that this course offering may be cancelled if fewer than 10 students enroll.

assessment_details.title: Peer Workshops
assessment_details.category: Participation/ Student contribution, Practical/ Demonstration, Presentation
assessment_details.due_date: Workshops will be held in timetabled Lab classes during Weeks 4, 5, and 6. From Week 3 onward, the allocated date is firm and can only be changed via an official extension request.
assessment_details.task_description: Facilitate a Workshop In a group of two, facilitate a 30-minute workshop during your scheduled lab class, introducing peers to a particular technology, app, or software. Timeline In Week 2: Self-allocate a workshop date and topic via the sign-up sheet. Before your allocated workshop date: Conduct independent research to thoroughly learn and understand the allocated technology. Plan an engaging 30-minute workshop session, including demonstrations, explanations, and interactivity. On your allocated workshop date: With your partner, facilitate a 30-minute workshop on your allocated topic. Take charge of timing, classroom engagement, and technology management. Submit your workshop plan to Blackboard. During Weeks 4, 5, and 6: Participate in classmates' workshops. Topics A range of workshop topics will be be available for allocation, including: * iPad Music Apps (e.g. Koala Sampler, ThumbJam, Loopy HD) * Music Hardware (e.g. Ableton Push, Korg Volca, Zoom H4n) * Music Software (e.g. Audacity, MuseScore, Live, Max for Live) * Free choice (consult with Tutor) Where topics are multi-faceted and complex (e.g. Ableton Live or Ableton Push), students should choose to focus on one aspect (e.g. multi-track recording in Ableton Live; Playing Drums on Ableton Push). Presentation and Submission Presentations must occur in-person on the allocated date with all group members present for the entire duration of the class. A workshop plan must be submitted on the day which details the main sections, talking points, and activities to be covered in the workshop; this may take the form of a document or slides. Students must attend and participate in at least one class of workshops other than the class in which they are scheduled to present in order to pass the "Participation" criterion. Marking Criteria * Operation 30% * Technical Understanding 30% * Communication 20% * Participation (in others' workshops) 20% This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submit your workshop plan (maximum 5 pages) to blackboard on your workshop date.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
If students are unable attend due to illness or other exceptional circumstance, they may apply for an extension. If approved, students may liaise with the course co-ordinator to negotiate an alternative date to complete the assessment. The alternative date must be suitable for the teaching staff. Students are responsible for following up to ensure suitable arrangements are made to complete the assessment.
Your extension application must be submitted on time, with appropriate evidence.
While your extension request is being considered, you should work towards completing and submitting your assessment as soon as possible.
A late penalty will be applied if you don't submit your assessment on time or if you don't have a valid reason for an extension.
Late submission
You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late .
This assessment is completed in-class according to a set schedule. Failing to deliver the scheduled workshop without an approved extension results in a mark of 0.

assessment_details.task_description: Each student will propose and complete a creative project using music technology. This will involve a creative output as well as a written exegesis. The assessment of this project is broken into four parts: a Project Proposal, Project Journals, Project Presentation , and Project Exegesis. Project Proposal Students submit a Project Proposal in Week 8 , setting out the project aims, technology to be used, and the skills required, using the template provided . This is a 10% graded assessment item. Project Journal 1 & 2 From Weeks 9 to 11 , students work on projects. With tutor’s guidance, the focus is on gaining the required skills and completing the creative work. During this time, students keep a Project Journal to help reflect on the project, submitting journal entries in Weeks 10 and 12. Each of these are a 5% pass/fail assessment item. Project Presentation Students present the creative output of your project to the class in the Week 13 Project Presentation. This must be done in person during the Week 13 class time*. This is a 30% graded assessment item. Project Exegesis Finally, students write and submit a 2000-word Project Exegesis . This is a scholarly work reflecting on the project and linking it to existing research. This is a 20% graded assessment item. *In the case of projects which do not suit in-class presentation, (e.g. a concert or sound installation), alternative arrangements must be made and agreed upon with the tutor and course co-ordinator.
